why_no_single_model_pass: The two local ASR models fail on different single tokens of the same bytes, so neither produces a clean read on its own. That is the limit of the automated gate, not a finding about the audio.

token_by_token_resolution.resolved_by: owner listening to the full sentence
token_by_token_resolution.strength: human ear on the exact disputed span

token_by_token_resolution.small_en: heard and written as the % symbol, which the declared percent_symbol allowance covers
token_by_token_resolution.strength: weaker than the band resolution. The owner did not listen to this token; it rests on small.en hearing it where medium.en did not. The two models never agree that a token is absent, and no token in this script is unattested by both.

conclusion: Every expected token of the 04 transfer source is attested. 'band' is settled by the owner's ear; 'percent' by small.en alone. Treated as sufficient to transfer, because the transfer preserves words rather than deciding them and the resulting Original C audio still faces owner listening before anything is built from it.
if_wrong: If 'seventy percent' is in fact missing from the audio it will be audible in the Original C result, and the short would need a new guide, a fresh Google call under fresh authority. Nothing downstream of the transfer is authorized, so the cost of being wrong is one transfer's credits.
limitations: ASR cannot prove an unclipped final phoneme. Nothing here establishes voice match, performance or register.
